PropertyKindCalculus.Uncertainty.Sensitivity.gradient (model : PropertyKindCalculus.Uncertainty.Sensitivity.ScalarModel) (point : List Float) : Except String (List Float)**Reverse-mode gradient of a scalar model at a point.** Instantiates the write-once kernel at the tape carrier `TapeBuilder .scalar`, creating one differentiable input leaf per coordinate of `point`, records the forward tape, runs a single reverse pass from the scalar output, and reads back `∂f/∂xᵢ` at `point` in input order. These are the sensitivity coefficients `cᵢ` the linearized GUM/Willink methods consume (UNCERTAINTY.md §3.2 item 1). **Stage 3.5 retarget.** The reverse pass is the *total dense* engine entry `Tape.backwardDenseFrom` — the very function TorchLean's soundness theorem `backwardDenseFrom_lowerGraphToTape_adjoint_fderiv` (`NN/Proofs/Autograd/Runtime/Link/FDeriv.lean`) characterizes: on a compiled graph at the `ℝ` carrier, its input-prefix output is the adjoint of the Fréchet derivative of the forward evaluation. The seed is `1` at the scalar output and `0` everywhere else, which on a topologically-ordered tape computes the same accumulation as the previous reachability-pruned `backwardScalar` path (a dead subexpression now contributes an exact `0` instead of being skipped). The two honest gaps that remain are recorded in UNCERTAINTY.md §3.2/§6: this tape is built eagerly rather than by `lowerGraphToTape` (provenance), and it runs at `Float` while the theorem speaks at `ℝ` (the deviation is this workstream's own Adequacy claim).

PropertyKindCalculus.WholeProper.{u} {O : Type u} (k : PropertyKindCalculus.KindOfProperty) (m : PropertyKindCalculus.Measurement O) : Prop**A whole-proper kind — the case Bunge's four types do not name.** The value of the whole is produced by *no* aggregation over the parts: neither by summing them (`notAdditive`) nor by sharing a common reading with them (`notUniform`). The normal-mode frequency of a coupled pair is the standard case — a lone oscillator has no normal mode at all, so there is nothing to sum and nothing to inherit. It is not §13.5.4 intensive: the value is not invariant with the extent of the system, since a third oscillator moves every mode. Both fields are **exhibited**, as pairs of atomic parts, rather than stated as negated universals. That is deliberate: a negated universal is satisfied by a measurement that is merely undefined somewhere, while a witness pins the failure to two parts a reader can point at — the same discipline `mixing_subadditive` follows for volume, and the reason `assemble` over such a kind can be shown to return the *wrong number* rather than merely an unjustified one (`assemble_ne_measured`, `Composite.lean`). This is Marmodoro's substantial power in the §13.5 vocabulary. Her structural powers constitute a whole out of parts — the aggregable kinds — while the substantial power "*is* the electron" (*Whole, but not One*, 2018, §4): borne by the whole, and not by anything the whole is made of.

Taking `b` at a part's own mass centre and `a` at the system's shows the split of an angular momentum into spin and orbital terms is this law and not a new principle — and a part whose momentum vanishes reads the same about every point, which is why a parked flywheel's spin may be summed untransported and a translating one's may not.

The whole `whole` and the part-injection `part` are arguments, so this serves a bespoke `Composite P` (`assemble σ .whole .part`) and equally a host library's own object type with its own naming of parts (`assemble σ rover (partOf rover)`). `f` is *dependent*: the quantity supplied for `p` must characterize `part p`, which is the gate — a part's quantity cannot be smuggled in under another part's name. The traversal is `Decomposition.fold`, the same one `leafSum` uses, so the arithmetic here and the §13.5 law are one recursion read at two carriers rather than two that agree.

This is what makes `Assembles` a claim about the world rather than a permission slip: the class licenses the sum to be *written*, and this theorem is what an author shows to say the sum is *right*. Its absence is exactly the volume-on-mixing case — `volMix` has no `Extensive` witness, so no instance of this theorem exists for it.

PropertyKindCalculus.assemble_ne_measured.{u, v} {O : Type u} {P : Type v} {k : PropertyKindCalculus.KindOfProperty} (σ : PropertyKindCalculus.SortOfSystem) [PropertyKindCalculus.Assembles σ k] (whole : O) (part : P → O) {m : PropertyKindCalculus.Measurement P} (h : PropertyKindCalculus.WholeProper k m) : ∃ d, (PropertyKindCalculus.assemble σ whole part d fun p => { magnitude := (m (PropertyKindCalculus.Decomposition.atom p)).numeral }).magnitude ≠ (m d).numeral**The license refused.** For a *whole-proper* kind — one whose value the parts do not determine, in either of the two ways they could — there is a carving on which the assembled magnitude is **not** the value the whole has. Not merely unjustified: wrong, on an exhibited pair of parts. The `[Assembles σ k]` instance is still required, and that is the finding. The class licenses the sum to be *written*; nothing about writing it makes it true, so an author who registers a whole-proper kind gets a term that elaborates and a number that is not the physics. This is the negative counterpart of `assemble_eq_measured` — same eliminator, same measurement, the `Extensive` hypothesis replaced by its refutation — and it is why the registry is opt-in and its entries are curated per sort.

PropertyKindCalculus.extensive_additive.{u} {O : Type u} {k : PropertyKindCalculus.KindOfProperty} {m : PropertyKindCalculus.Measurement O} (h : PropertyKindCalculus.Extensive k m) (d : PropertyKindCalculus.Decomposition O) : (m d).numeral = PropertyKindCalculus.leafSum m d**Extensive aggregation (the capstone).** For an extensive kind, the value measured on the *whole* equals the sum over *all* atomic parts of a decomposition, $$`\mathrm{value}\Bigl(\bigsqcup_i s_i\Bigr) = \sum_i \mathrm{value}(s_i),` to arbitrary depth. The $`\forall`-quantified law itself — not a single instance — is the deliverable: it is proved by induction on the decomposition, lifting the single-split `additive` field to the whole tree.

PropertyKindCalculus.intensive_uniform.{u} {O : Type u} {k : PropertyKindCalculus.KindOfProperty} {m : PropertyKindCalculus.Measurement O} {v : ℤ} (h : PropertyKindCalculus.Intensive k m) (d : PropertyKindCalculus.Decomposition O) : PropertyKindCalculus.Decomposition.Forall (fun s => (m (PropertyKindCalculus.Decomposition.atom s)).numeral = v) d → (m d).numeral = v**Intensive aggregation (the capstone).** For an intensive kind, a whole *all* of whose atomic parts read `v` reads `v` itself — to arbitrary depth, over any carving, proved by induction on the decomposition exactly as `extensive_additive` is. The two capstones are the same theorem at two aggregation modes, which is the point of stating both: `Extensive` sends the leaves to a sum, `Intensive` sends a *uniform* family of leaves to its common value, and a kind that does neither is not thereby unmeasurable — it is `WholeProper` below.

The second hypothesis is that `toSpec` reflects zero — it sends only the exec zero to the spec zero. Every refinement in this library has it; it is stated rather than assumed because a lossy `toSpec` that collapsed a subnormal to zero would not.

PropertyKindCalculus.mixing_subadditive : (PropertyKindCalculus.volMix PropertyKindCalculus.mixture).numeral < (PropertyKindCalculus.volMix PropertyKindCalculus.waterPart).numeral + (PropertyKindCalculus.volMix PropertyKindCalculus.ethanolPart).numeral ∧ ¬PropertyKindCalculus.Extensive PropertyKindCalculus.volume PropertyKindCalculus.volMix**Volume on mixing is not extensive.** The mixture's volume is *strictly less* than the sum of the component volumes (96 < 50 + 50), so additivity fails and `volume` is not extensive under this measurement. Matching the extensive law would be unsound here — which is exactly why extensivity must be tracked, not assumed.

PropertyKindCalculus.momentumBoost.{u} {O : Type u} (w v : O → ℤ) (u₁ u₂ : ℤ) (d : PropertyKindCalculus.Decomposition O) : PropertyKindCalculus.momentumIn w v u₁ d = PropertyKindCalculus.momentumIn w v u₂ d + PropertyKindCalculus.partTotal w d * (u₂ - u₁)**The Galilean boost, as a transport law**: the momentum read in the frame at `u₁` is the momentum read at `u₂` plus the carving's mass times the frame difference — the correction is the one unconditionally extensive summary there is, which is the tower's ground floor.
PropertyKindCalculus.momentumIn.{u} {O : Type u} (w v : O → ℤ) (u : ℤ) : PropertyKindCalculus.Decomposition O → ℤ**Momentum read in the frame moving at `u`**: `∑ wᵢ (vᵢ − u)`, as a fold.

PropertyKindCalculus.netTotal_union.{u} {O : Type u} (act : O → O → ℤ) (ext : O → ℤ) (a b : PropertyKindCalculus.Decomposition O) : PropertyKindCalculus.netTotal act ext (a.union b) = PropertyKindCalculus.netTotal act ext a + PropertyKindCalculus.netTotal act ext b + (PropertyKindCalculus.mutualTotal act a b + PropertyKindCalculus.mutualTotal act b a)**The exact price of additivity** — for *any* pairwise action, lawful or not. Rolling up per-part nets over a union overshoots the two halves' own rollups by precisely the two cross-flows over the cut. Everything the antisymmetric layer proves is this identity with the price argued to zero; everything a lawless table gets wrong is this identity with the price left standing.
O → O → ℤ

PropertyKindCalculus.mutualTotal.{u} {O : Type u} (act : O → O → ℤ) (a b : PropertyKindCalculus.Decomposition O) : ℤ**What one carving exerts on another, in total** — the flow across the cut between them: every `a`-leaf-to-`b`-leaf entry, read once.

PropertyKindCalculus.normalMode_wholeProper : PropertyKindCalculus.WholeProper PropertyKindCalculus.oscillatorFrequency PropertyKindCalculus.normalModeFreq**The pair's normal-mode frequency is whole-proper.** 14 is not 10 + 10, and 14 is not the parts' shared 10: the value belongs to the pair and is inherited from neither part.

PropertyKindCalculus.oscillatorFrequency : PropertyKindCalculus.KindOfPropertyAngular frequency, a ratio kind — the *generic* kind the parts and the whole share. What distinguishes the pair's reading is its dedication (*"coupled oscillator pair — normal mode + ; angular frequency"*), not the kind-of-property, which is why the failure below is a fact about aggregation and not about commensurability.

PropertyKindCalculus.normalModeFreq : PropertyKindCalculus.Measurement PropertyKindCalculus.SystemThe frequency measurement of the coupled pair: each oscillator alone reads ω₀ = 10 rad/s, the pair reads its upper normal mode ω₊ = 14 rad/s.

PropertyKindCalculus.not_extensive_of_intensive.{u} {O : Type u} {k : PropertyKindCalculus.KindOfProperty} {m : PropertyKindCalculus.Measurement O} (hi : PropertyKindCalculus.Intensive k m) {a b : PropertyKindCalculus.Decomposition O} (hab : (m a).numeral = (m b).numeral) (hne : (m a).numeral ≠ 0) : ¬PropertyKindCalculus.Extensive k m**The two branches exclude each other, wherever there is anything to measure.** An intensive kind is not extensive as soon as two parts agree on a *nonzero* value: additivity would double it, constancy keeps it, and only `0 = 0 + 0` satisfies both. The zero escape is not a defect of the statement — it is the observation that a kind whose every reading is zero satisfies both laws vacuously, which is why the hypothesis is stated rather than assumed away.
(m a).numeral = (m b).numeral
(m a).numeral ≠ 0

PropertyKindCalculus.parallelAxis.{u} {O : Type u} (w x : O → ℤ) (a b : ℤ) (d : PropertyKindCalculus.Decomposition O) : PropertyKindCalculus.inertiaAbout w x a d = PropertyKindCalculus.inertiaAbout w x b d + (2 * (b - a) * PropertyKindCalculus.firstMoment w x d + (a * a - b * b) * PropertyKindCalculus.partTotal w d)**The parallel-axis theorem, over any carving of any part type.** The moment of inertia about `a` is the moment about `b` plus a correction built from the carving's *first moment* and its *total mass* — two extensive summaries of the same parts. Taking `b` at the centre of mass makes the first moment vanish and leaves the textbook `M d²`. Proved by induction on the carving: at a leaf it is `ring` on `w·(x−a)² = w·(x−b)² + 2(b−a)·w·x + (a²−b²)·w`, and at a join the three folds distribute.
PropertyKindCalculus.inertiaAbout.{u} {O : Type u} (w x : O → ℤ) (a : ℤ) : PropertyKindCalculus.Decomposition O → ℤ**The moment of inertia about the axis at `a`**: `∑ wᵢ (xᵢ − a)²`, as a fold.

PropertyKindCalculus.reynolds_ne_mach_but_both_dimensionless : PropertyKindCalculus.reynoldsK.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ≠ PropertyKindCalculus.machK.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ∧ PropertyKindCalculus.reynoldsK.toDimension = 1 ∧ PropertyKindCalculus.machK.toDimension = 1**A characteristic number is a kind, not a constant.** Reynolds and Mach are *distinct kinds* though both forget to dimension one — a dimension-only system identifies them, the kind layer keeps them apart. Unlike `MathCarrier.pi` (a fixed magnitude in the carrier), each is a variable quantity formed by the quotient calculus; the value of a Reynolds number is whatever `ρvL/μ` produces in a given flow.
PropertyKindCalculus.reynoldsK : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseReynolds number — a dimension-one ratio kind (`ρvL/μ`, inertial over viscous forces).
PropertyKindCalculus.machK : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseMach number — a dimension-one ratio kind (flow speed over speed of sound).

PropertyKindCalculus.sqrt_area_coherent : PropertyKindCalculus.DimPowerKind (1 / 2) PropertyKindCalculus.areaK PropertyKindCalculus.lengthKind**`sqrt` of an area is a length — checked, not annotated.** The half-power of the area dimension `L²` is the length dimension `L`: `dim(√area) = (dim area)^(1/2) = L`. This is the certificate the core `Quantity.sqrt` carries, here discharged in the `Dimension` group.

PropertyKindCalculus.DimPowerKind (p : ℚ) (a b : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBase) : Prop**The dimensional power law.** `b` is the `p`-th power of `a` at the dimension level: its dimension is `a`'s scaled by `p`. The `Dimension`-layer strengthening of the core `PowerKind`'s ratio-scale gate.
PropertyKindCalculus.areaK : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseArea, a dimensionful ratio kind (`L²`) — the worked base for the half-power.
PropertyKindCalculus.lengthKind : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseLength, a dimensionful ratio kind.

PropertyKindCalculus.torque_angle_work : PropertyKindCalculus.siMech.KMul PropertyKindCalculus.torqueKind PropertyKindCalculus.angleKind PropertyKindCalculus.energyKind ∧ PropertyKindCalculus.energyKind.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ≠ PropertyKindCalculus.torqueKind.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ∧ PropertyKindCalculus.energyKind.toDimension = PropertyKindCalculus.torqueKind.toDimension**Worked instance — torque × plane-angle = energy, and energy is not torque.** The product is sanctioned, yet `energy ≠ torque` as kinds even though `dim energy = dim torque`. This is the small example carrying exactly the information dimensional analysis discards: the algebra distinguishes a moment from the work it does.

PropertyKindCalculus.siMech : PropertyKindCalculus.InteractionAlgebraThe worked SI-mechanics algebra packaged as a coherent `InteractionAlgebra`: the curated relation together with its discharged coherence obligation. An application declares its own algebra exactly like this — by listing products and proving each coheres.
PropertyKindCalculus.torqueKind : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseTorque, a ratio kind of dimension `M·L²·T⁻²` — the *same dimension* as `energyKind`, a *different* kind.
PropertyKindCalculus.angleKind : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBasePlane angle, a ratio kind of dimension one (Dybkær: a dimensionless quantity).
PropertyKindCalculus.energyKind : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseEnergy / work, a ratio kind of dimension `M·L²·T⁻²`.
